import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup layout
        title = "Defining Rigor: The Epsilon-Delta Challenge"
        lines = [
            "Let's define the limit with mathematical precision.",
            "Epsilon sets a vertical target window around the limit.",
            "Can we find a horizontal window for our inputs?",
            "This delta window ensures all outputs stay inside epsilon.",
            "If it works for any epsilon, the limit exists."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        eps_color = "#FFD700"
        delta_color = "#00BFFF"
        white = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(white))
        
        # Create Axes and Graph
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 3, 1],
            y_range=[0, 3, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": white}
        )
        # Define a smooth curve: f(x) = 0.5x^2 + 0.5
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2 + 0.5, x_range=[0.2, 2.5], color=white)
        
        # Target Point (c, L) where c = 1.5, L = 0.5(1.5)^2 + 0.5 = 1.625
        c_val = 1.5
        L_val = 1.625
        target_point = Dot(axes.c2p(c_val, L_val), color=white)
        
        # Visual lines for c and L
        c_line = axes.get_vertical_line(axes.c2p(c_val, L_val), color=white)
        L_line = axes.get_horizontal_line(axes.c2p(c_val, L_val), color=white)
        
        # Fixed FileNotFoundError by replacing MathTex with Text (removes LaTeX dependency)
        c_label = Text("c", font_size=24, color=white).move_to(axes.c2p(c_val, -0.3))
        L_label = Text("L", font_size=24, color=white).move_to(axes.c2p(-0.3, L_val))
        
        # Group and place in area A1 to F6
        graph_elements = VGroup(axes, curve, target_point, c_line, L_line, c_label, L_label)
        self.place_in_area(graph_elements, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.play(FadeIn(target_point), Create(c_line), Create(L_line), Write(c_label), Write(L_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(eps_color))
        
        # Epsilon tolerance around L
        epsilon = 0.5
        y_top = L_val + epsilon
        y_bottom = L_val - epsilon
        
        # Calculate dimensions in MUs
        eps_band_height = abs(axes.c2p(0, y_top)[1] - axes.c2p(0, y_bottom)[1])
        eps_band_width = abs(axes.c2p(2.8, 0)[0] - axes.c2p(0.2, 0)[0])
        
        eps_band = Rectangle(
            width=eps_band_width, 
            height=eps_band_height,
            fill_color=eps_color,
            fill_opacity=0.2,
            stroke_width=0
        ).move_to(axes.c2p(1.5, L_val))
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text for epsilon symbols
        L_plus_eps = Text("L + ε", font_size=20, color=eps_color).move_to(axes.c2p(-0.7, y_top))
        L_minus_eps = Text("L - ε", font_size=20, color=eps_color).move_to(axes.c2p(-0.7, y_bottom))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(eps_band), Write(L_plus_eps), Write(L_minus_eps))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(delta_color))
        
        # Delta window around c
        delta = 0.3
        x_right = c_val + delta
        x_left = c_val - delta
        
        delta_band_width = abs(axes.c2p(x_right, 0)[0] - axes.c2p(x_left, 0)[0])
        delta_band_height = abs(axes.c2p(0, 2.8)[1] - axes.c2p(0, 0.2)[1])
        
        delta_band = Rectangle(
            width=delta_band_width,
            height=delta_band_height,
            fill_color=delta_color,
            fill_opacity=0.2,
            stroke_width=0
        ).move_to(axes.c2p(c_val, 1.5))
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text for delta symbols
        c_plus_delta = Text("c + δ", font_size=20, color=delta_color).move_to(axes.c2p(x_right, -0.3))
        c_minus_delta = Text("c - δ", font_size=20, color=delta_color).move_to(axes.c2p(x_left, -0.3))

        self.play(FadeIn(delta_band), Write(c_plus_delta), Write(c_minus_delta))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(white))
        
        # Highlight the rectangular intersection
        intersection_rect = Rectangle(
            width=delta_band_width,
            height=eps_band_height,
            color=white,
            stroke_width=2
        ).move_to(axes.c2p(c_val, L_val))
        
        self.play(Create(intersection_rect))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(white))
        
        # Shrink the Epsilon band and the Delta band
        new_epsilon = 0.25
        new_delta = 0.15 
        
        new_eps_height = abs(axes.c2p(0, L_val + new_epsilon)[1] - axes.c2p(0, L_val - new_epsilon)[1])
        new_delta_width = abs(axes.c2p(c_val + new_delta, 0)[0] - axes.c2p(c_val - new_delta, 0)[0])
        
        self.play(
            eps_band.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(new_eps_height).move_to(axes.c2p(1.5, L_val)),
            delta_band.animate.stretch_to_fit_width(new_delta_width).move_to(axes.c2p(c_val, 1.5)),
            intersection_rect.animate.stretch_to_fit_width(new_delta_width).stretch_to_fit_height(new_eps_height).move_to(axes.c2p(c_val, L_val)),
            L_plus_eps.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(-0.7, L_val + new_epsilon)),
            L_minus_eps.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(-0.7, L_val - new_epsilon)),
            c_plus_delta.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(c_val + new_delta, -0.3)),
            c_minus_delta.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(c_val - new_delta, -0.3)),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Mandatory call to setup_layout with section title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "When Limits Fail: Indeterminate Forms", 
            [
                "Expressions like zero over zero are math stalemates.",
                "Both parts shrink, so we cannot determine the winner.",
                "Standard substitution fails, signaling we need better tools."
            ]
        )

        # Initialize lecture opacity
        for line in self.lecture:
            line.set_opacity(0.3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_opacity(1))
        
        # Build x/x limit expression using Text and Lines to avoid LaTeX dependencies
        lim_word = Text("lim", font_size=36)
        sub_text = Text("x → 0", font_size=18).next_to(lim_word, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        lim_part = VGroup(lim_word, sub_text)
        
        num = Text("x", font_size=36)
        den = Text("x", font_size=36)
        frac_line = Line(LEFT*0.3, RIGHT*0.3, stroke_width=2)
        fraction = VGroup(num, frac_line, den).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        equals = Text("=", font_size=36)
        zero_zero = VGroup(
            Text("0", font_size=36, color=RED),
            Line(LEFT*0.3, RIGHT*0.3, stroke_width=2, color=RED),
            Text("0", font_size=36, color=RED)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)

        expression = VGroup(lim_part, fraction, equals, zero_zero).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(expression, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(expression[0:2]))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(Write(expression[2:]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_opacity(1)
        )
        
        question_mark = Text("?", font_size=60, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(question_mark, "D3")
        
        arrow_num = Arrow(start=expression[1][0].get_top(), end=expression[1][0].get_top()+UP*0.5, color=BLUE)
        arrow_den = Arrow(start=expression[1][2].get_bottom(), end=expression[1][2].get_bottom()+DOWN*0.5, color=BLUE)
        shrinking_label = Text("Both vanish", font_size=20, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(shrinking_label, "D5")

        self.play(Create(arrow_num), Create(arrow_den), Write(question_mark))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_opacity(1)
        )
        
        tool_text = Text("Need L'Hôpital or Algebra", font_size=24, color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(tool_text, "E3")
        
        self.play(Write(tool_text))
        self.play(Indicate(tool_text))
        self.wait(2)

        # Reset all opacities for conclusion
        self.play(self.lecture.animate.set_opacity(1))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initializing the layout for Section 4
        self.setup_layout(
            "L'Hôpital's Rule: Solving Indeterminate Forms",
            [
                "- Indeterminate Forms: 0/0 and ∞/∞",
                "- Rule: lim f(x)/g(x) = lim f'(x)/g'(x)",
                "- Visualizing the ratio of rates",
                "- Example: lim[x→0] sin(x)/x",
                "- Derivatives: sin'(x)=cos(x), x'=1"
            ]
        )

        # Math Objects - Replaced MathTex with Text to resolve 'latex' executable missing error
        limit_problem = Text("lim[x→0] sin(x)/x", color=BLUE, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(limit_problem, "B3", scale_factor=1.2)

        lhopital_step = Text("= lim[x→0] (d/dx sin(x)) / (d/dx x)", color=YELLOW, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(lhopital_step, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)

        derivative_step = Text("= lim[x→0] cos(x) / 1", color=GREEN, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(derivative_step, "D3", scale_factor=1.2)

        final_answer = Text("= 1", color=WHITE, font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(final_answer, "E3", scale_factor=1.5)

        # Animation Sequence
        self.play(Write(limit_problem))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(lhopital_step, shift=DOWN))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(lhopital_step.copy(), derivative_step))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(Write(final_answer))
        self.wait(3)

        # Highlighting the conclusion
        box = SurroundingRectangle(final_answer, color=YELLOW, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.wait(2)

        # Line: "Limits range from visual paths to rigorous error bounds."
        # Visual: Show the Robo-Ant crossing the graph's hole.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(ANT_COLOR))
        
        # Position axes in the right-side grid system area
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-0.5, 4, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": WHITE},
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=3.5
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E6")
        
        # Plot a curve with a hole at x=0
        graph = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2 + 1, x_range=[-2, 2], color=WHITE)
        
        # The Hole (pothole) visual representation
        hole_pos = axes.c2p(0, 1)
        hole_circle = Circle(radius=0.1, color=HOLE_COLOR).move_to(hole_pos)
        hole_fill = Dot(hole_pos, color=BLACK, radius=0.11)
        
        # Robo-Ant group (Ant + Label)
        ant_dot = Dot(color=ANT_COLOR, radius=0.15)
        ant_name = Text("Robo-Ant", font_size=16, color=ANT_COLOR).next_to(ant_dot, UP, buff=0.1)
        robo_ant = VGroup(ant_dot, ant_name)
        
        # Set starting position for the ant
        robo_ant.move_to(axes.c2p(-1.8, 1.8**2 + 1))
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(graph))
        self.play(Create(hole_circle), Create(hole_fill))
        self.add(robo_ant)
        
        # Moving along the path to simulate crossing the gap
        path = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2 + 1, x_range=[-1.8, 1.8])
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(robo_ant, path), run_time=4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line: "Derivatives provide a shortcut for tough indeterminate forms."
        # Visual: Pulse the Epsilon-Delta box in the background representing the rigorous tool.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(EPSILON_COLOR))
        
        # Epsilon-Delta "Safety Window" box around the hole
        ed_box = Rectangle(
            width=1.4, height=1.0, 
            color=EPSILON_COLOR, 
            fill_color=DELTA_COLOR, 
            fill_opacity=0.3
        ).move_to(hole_pos)
        
        # Derivative shortcut label (Visualizing the 'Derivative Speedometer' concept)
        deriv_shortcut = Text("dy/dx Shortcut", font_size=18, color=ANT_COLOR).next_to(robo_ant, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(ed_box), FadeIn(deriv_shortcut))
        self.play(
            ed_box.animate.scale(1.25),
            run_time=0.75,
            rate_func=there_and_back
        )
        self.play(
            ed_box.animate.scale(1.25),
            run_time=0.75,
            rate_func=there_and_back
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line: "Mastery of limits builds the foundation for all calculus."
        # Visual: Fade into final text 'Limits: The Destination'
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(FINAL_TEXT_COLOR))
        
        final_text_obj = Text("Limits: The Destination", font_size=36, color=FINAL_TEXT_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(final_text_obj, "B1", "E6")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(graph), FadeOut(hole_circle), 
            FadeOut(hole_fill), FadeOut(robo_ant), FadeOut(ed_box),
            FadeOut(deriv_shortcut)
        )
        self.play(Write(final_text_obj))
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Essence of Limits: From Visual Intuition to L'Hôpital's Rule

sections.title: The Intuition: The 'Almost' Point
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a limit as a destination rather than a location. Explain that a limit describes what happens to a function as the input gets 'arbitrarily close' to a value, even if the function is undefined there. Prerequisite: Understanding of basic function notation f(x).
sections.example: Animate a 'Robo-Ant' walking along the graph of f(x) = (x^2 - 1)/(x - 1). As the ant approaches x = 1, it encounters a tiny 'pothole' (hole in the graph). Even though it can't step on x = 1, we can see it is heading toward the height of y = 2.

sections.title: Defining Rigor: The Epsilon-Delta Challenge
sections.content: Transition from intuition to the formal definition. Introduce Epsilon (ε) as the 'Vertical Error Tolerance' and Delta (δ) as the 'Horizontal Input Window'. Explain the logic: For any error margin ε someone gives you, you can find a safety window δ such that the function stays within that margin.
sections.example: Visual: A 'Precision Game'. A player sets a horizontal neon band of width 2ε around the target height L. The instructional designer must then find a vertical 'safe zone' of width 2δ such that every part of the graph within δ stays inside the ε band.

sections.title: When Limits Fail: Indeterminate Forms
sections.content: Introduce the problem of 0/0 or ∞/∞. Explain that these are 'math stalemates' where the numerator and denominator are both fighting to reach a limit, but we can't tell who wins by simple substitution. Prerequisite: Basic understanding of slopes and derivatives.
sections.example: Show a fraction as a tug-of-war between two characters: 'Numerator' and 'Denominator'. In the limit of sin(x)/x as x approaches 0, both characters shrink to zero simultaneously. The screen shows a 'Calculation Error' pop-up to signify the need for a better tool.

sections.title: The Solution: L'Hôpital's Rule
sections.content: Present L'Hôpital's Rule as a comparison of 'speeds'. If both the top and bottom are heading to zero, their ratio is determined by how fast they are changing—which is their derivative. Formula: lim [f(x)/g(x)] = lim [f'(x)/g'(x)].
sections.example: Animate two cars (f and g) racing toward a finish line at x = c. At the finish line, both cars' positions are 0. To see who was 'winning' right before they hit zero, we look at their speedometers (derivatives f' and g') at that exact moment.

sections.title: Synthesis and Application
sections.content: Briefly recap the journey: from the visual 'pothole' to the rigorous ε-δ definition, and finally the L'Hôpital shortcut for complex indeterminate forms. Emphasize that L'Hôpital's Rule only works for specific indeterminate forms.
sections.example: A summary graphic showing the 'Robo-Ant' from Section 1 now using a 'Derivative Speedometer' to cross the '0/0 pothole' safely, while the ε-δ 'Safety Window' glows in the background to represent the underlying rigorous foundation.

storyboard.title: The Intuition: The 'Almost' Point
lecture_lines: A limit describes where a function is headed.
Imagine an ant walking along this graph.
At x equals 1, there is a tiny pothole.
The ant can't step there, but follows the path.
Its destination is clearly at height y equals 2.
animations: Display the formula f(x) = (x^2 - 1)/(x - 1) in #FFFFFF at the top.
Draw a straight line in #FFFFFF representing y = x + 1 (the simplified function).
Place the Robo-Ant [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ant.svg] on the line at x = 0.5.
Animate the Robo-Ant [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ant.svg] moving smoothly along the line towards x = 1.
Reveal a small #FF0000 hollow circle (the hole) at the point (1, 2).

storyboard.title: Defining Rigor: The Epsilon-Delta Challenge
lecture_lines: Let's define the limit with mathematical precision.
Epsilon sets a vertical target window around the limit.
Can we find a horizontal window for our inputs?
This delta window ensures all outputs stay inside epsilon.
If it works for any epsilon, the limit exists.
animations: Draw a smooth curve in #FFFFFF with a target point (c, L) labeled.
Overlay a horizontal #FFD700 (yellow) band representing the Epsilon (ε) tolerance around L.
Overlay a vertical #00BFFF (blue) band representing the Delta (δ) window around c.
Highlight the rectangular intersection of the two bands with a #FFFFFF border.
Shrink the Epsilon band and animate the Delta band shrinking to keep the curve within the intersection.

storyboard.title: When Limits Fail: Indeterminate Forms
lecture_lines: Expressions like zero over zero are math stalemates.
Both parts shrink, so we cannot determine the winner.
Standard substitution fails, signaling we need better tools.
animations: Display the limit expression lim(x->0) sin(x)/x in #FFFFFF.
Animate 'sin(x)' and 'x' both turning #FF0000 and shrinking as x approaches 0.
Replace the entire expression with a large, flashing #FF0000 '0/0' symbol.

storyboard.title: The Solution: L'Hôpital's Rule
lecture_lines: L'Hôpital's Rule compares how fast the functions change.
Imagine two cars racing toward the same finish line.
Both reach zero, but their speeds determine the ratio.
We compare the derivatives of the top and bottom.
The limit of their speeds reveals the final answer.
animations: Display L'Hopital's Rule formula: lim f(x)/g(x) = lim f'(x)/g'(x) in #FFFFFF.
Show two vertical bars, Green (f) and Blue (g), both decreasing to zero height.
Transform the bars into two tangent arrows representing their derivatives (speeds) f' and g'.
Label the arrows with their respective derivative values in #00FF00 and #00BFFF.
Show the ratio of these values as the final limit result.

storyboard.title: Synthesis and Application
lecture_lines: Limits range from visual paths to rigorous error bounds.
Derivatives provide a shortcut for tough indeterminate forms.
Mastery of limits builds the foundation for all calculus.
animations: Show the Robo-Ant [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ant.svg] crossing the graph's hole (#FF0000).
Pulse the Epsilon-Delta box (#FFD700/#00BFFF) in the background.
Fade into the final text 'Limits: The Destination' in #FFFFFF.
